Across the internet there are bots absolutely everywhere (The Guardian has a great article about this), they are trolls that try to change opinion. Well if a comment is upvoted, people tend to think most people find that particular comment to be the best.. someone can make a bunch of accounts, use various browsers, even create virtual machines with different IP's to troll / bot.

I think requiring someone to have 100 contribution points really helps eliminate boting but if you leave it up to individual subverse, they likely wont use that rule thus you get trolls or whoever boting the upvotes/downvotes.

Also, having comments that are downvoted to oblivian essentially hides that comment. Most comment tools / sites like YouTube and Disqus don't hide comments like Reddit.

Bottom line: Have a mandatory amount of contribution points, dont allow comments to be hidden if they're voted down to oblivion. Take measures to fight against bots and trolls.

Electric Cars Can Be Worse For The Environment Than Gas Cars

It seems that the blame is on the source of energy, the coal fired power plants.

I commend the author for remaining unbiased throughout most of the article.

Does anyone have any data on what times of day these cars are being charged? If, for example, they are charged mostly at night, then the power use baseline will rise, and the power use baseline is powered nearly entirely by nuclear powerplants.

However, if they are charged at sporadic and inconsistent times throughout the day, then yes the power increase caused by the cars would be supplied by coal power plants.

It's not just that, it's also that electric vehicles have different efficiency characteristics than gas vehicles. EVs perform much better than GVs in things like stop-and-start traffic where idling is a factor, manual transmissions can lead to over-compensation and regenerative braking options (for EVs that have them) are at their most useful. These advantages don't apply to longer trips, where you're mostly looking at continuous highway travel and some EVs may suffer performance issues caused by operating at the extremes of their range. The really interesting thing about this study is that (assuming they didn't screw up somewhere else along the way) it gives a more tangible idea of how EV efficiency differs by environment and usage case.

In the end, you're right that the real blame belongs to the power infrastructure, but it's also important to be aware of the more direct differences between EVs and GVs.
Yeah I agree. The comparison between environments is where the study stands out.

It also depends how they are used and how long their life cycle is compared to internal combustion engine cars. If used in regions of lots of stop and go driving, and the vehicle and it's batteries have a long service life then they should in theory have a much smaller carbon foot print. Now if an EV is made disposable like Apple products then yah it would be worse for the environment even if they were recycled.

That seems like a fluff piece sponsored by oil companies that they distribute with Bibles or something. Very light on the details. Sure, electric cars contribute indirectly to carbon-footprints because it of the oil they use to produce the electric batteries, but where else am I seeing it? Tires, which gas-powered cars use too? electric cars contribute indirectly to carbon-footprints because it of the oil they use to produce the electric batteries

These raw materials have to be shipped all around the planet. Also there is the problem of recycling those wonders of technology once they are trashed. There are still countless problems with having electric cars on a grand scale. Not that I am in any way promoting gas cars..

I'm afraid the only real green car is called a bike.

This is a disingenous article and probably pushed by the oil/gas industry. Electric cars are ALL about the source that feeds them.
